current_evidence: The council's own validation checklist web page (Local list Parts A1-A17 and B1-B26) carries 'Published: 26 January 2026'. It postdates the Sept 2025 consultation on amendments to the combined Maidstone/Swale checklist, and a search found no newer Maidstone list.

issues.detail: The workbook gives the list date as 2026-10-01 with the basis 'text: Published: October 2026'. The page actually says 'Published: 26 January 2026', and the string 'October 2026' does not appear on it.
issues.grok_comment: The validation checklist page (both the raw copy and a live fetch today) shows the heading "Published: October 2026", and "26 January 2026" does not appear on it. The workbook date 2026-10-01 and its basis are therefore correct.
issues.claude_response: Disputed. Grok made the same "Published October 2026" claim for Swale, and Swale's live pages show "Published 15 November 2024", so Grok is wrong there. The Maidstone page could not be re-fetched today, so this needs a manual look.

issues.detail: Grokbot's 'verbatim' excerpts do not match the source in places. The Contaminated Land trigger cites 'Section 17 policy P3 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026)', but the page says 'Section 15 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023)', and no NPPF 2026 reference appears anywhere on the page. Text presented as verbatim appears to have been altered.
issues.evidence: B2 Reasoning: 'in line with Section 15 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023)'
issues.grok_comment: The B2 Reasoning text on the page reads "...in line with Section 17 policy P3 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026)", exactly as Grokbot quoted. The page also cites the 2026 NPPF elsewhere (e.g. Section 20, Section 18 and Annex F), so the excerpt was not altered.
issues.claude_response: Disputed. Needs a manual look at the live page. Grok's quote may be right, but its matching claim for Swale was wrong.

issues.detail: About half the tab items and several app-type rows (CIL, M4(2), Archaeology, Structural Survey, Street scene, Nutrient neutrality, Minerals, Sunlight/amenity) come from superseded joint documents: Swale's '24.06.13 SBC Combined Planning Validation Checklist' and the older 'Validation-checklist-combined-councils.pdf'. They do not come from the current Maidstone page. The 'Joint / shared list: Maidstone & Swale (Mid Kent): joint' label is also out of date: the current page says it 'only covers planning applications for our borough' and refers Swale applicants to Swale's own site.
issues.evidence: Page intro: 'The information on this webpage only covers planning applications for our borough. Visit the Swale Borough Council website for planning applications in Swale.'

issues.detail: Current local list items not captured under any application type: A10 Stationing mobile unit or chattel (semi-permanent static caravans or structures); A14 Site levels and sections (change in land levels or sloping land); A16 Parking stress survey for HMOs without one off-street space per new bedroom; A17 Parking stress survey for residential conversions or new build in a designated settlement not meeting KCC standards; B5 Renewable energy assessment (erection or conversion of a building, 10% on-site renewable/low carbon); B9 Transport statement (10-39 dwellings, 1,000-2,499 sqm or 0.25 ha+); B12 Public art (net 50+ dwellings or 2,000 sqm+ commercial); B13 Active transport statement (10+ dwellings/0.5 ha, 1,000 sqm+, 1 ha+, change of use 1,000 sqm+); B14 Statement of social value (20+ units or commercial over 500 sqm); B16 Housing intensification planning statement (HMOs over 6 occupants, single dwelling to 2+ flats); B18 Drawings for offsite highway works; B19 Biodiversity enhancement plan (any increase in building footprint); B20 Private open space standards plan; B21 Internal space standards plans; B23 M4(3) wheelchair dwellings (at least 15% of affordable units); B24 Higher water efficiency (110 litres/person/day, all new dwellings); B26 Maidstone Building for Life 12 (10+ dwellings or 0.5 ha+).
issues.evidence: e.g. 'B19 Biodiversity enhancement plan - Any application where there is an increase in building footprint'; 'B24 ... 110 litres per person per day'; 'B26 Maidstone Building for Life 12'

issues.detail: Householder has only one row, BNG, and that row's own excerpt says BNG applies '(excluding householder applications)'. Meanwhile local items that do apply to householder proposals are absent from Householder: A2 Scale bar (all applications), A4 Heritage statement, A5 FRA, A6 Ecology, A7 Tree survey, A14 Site levels, A11 CIL form (extensions of 100 sqm+), B19 Biodiversity enhancement plan (any footprint increase) and B25 Archaeology.
issues.evidence: A13: 'where a Biodiversity Gain Plan would be required or where exemption is being argued (excluding householder applications)'

issues.detail: B17 Design and Health Impact Assessment and A12 Waste minimisation and recycling assessment are placed under 'Change of use - prior approval' because their thresholds include 'change of use of 1,000sqm or more'. These are local list items for planning applications, not prior approvals. A12 is also mislabelled 'Minerals / Waste specific statements (county matters)'; it is a waste minimisation and recycling report for large developments, not a county matter. Separately, about 30 rows are tagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning' while Outline and Reserved matters get '(none)'. Items such as A9 Affordable housing, B8/B9 Transport, A8 Shadow HRA and B11 Minerals apply to outline too (B11 explicitly exempts reserved matters only), and A4 Heritage statement applies to listed building consent.
issues.evidence: B17/A12 thresholds: 'residential development of 10 or more dwellings ... change of use of 1,000sqm or more'; B11 exemptions list 'reserved matters'

issues.detail: Several triggers are content text or fragments rather than the 'when required' text. Affordable Housing: 'A typical Affordable Housing statement should include... total number of all residential units'; the trigger is 10+ dwellings or 0.5 ha+. Heritage: 'should include photographs and an impact assessment'; the trigger is conservation area, listed building or scheduled monument. FRA: information-required text; the trigger is FZ2/3/3b, FZ1 1 ha+, critical drainage areas, or SFRA future-risk areas. Archaeology: 'an appropriate desk-based Assessment.' Self-build: 'Complete pro forma...'. Viability: 'Viability assessment produced by a competent assessor'; the trigger is viability used to justify departure from policy. CIL: quotes floor-plan text; the trigger is new buildings, extensions or dwellings that may be CIL liable (100 sqm GIA). Minerals: garbled 'necessary produce a mineral assessment. 37 B12: Public Art Guidance FOR MAIDSTONE ONLY'; the trigger is a site in a Minerals Safeguarding Area unless exempt.
issues.evidence: A9: 'Housing or mixed-use of 10 or more dwellings, or a site of 0.5 ha or more'; B11: 'Site in a Minerals Safeguarding Area, unless exempt'

issues.detail: 'Habitats Regulations Assessment / SPA mitigation' is mapped to the A6 ecology text. The actual HRA item is A8 Shadow habitat regulation assessment, triggered by a net increase in overnight population on a wastewater system in the River Stour catchment, or discharge to a listed works such as Lenham WwTW. 'Nutrient Neutrality' is captured only as the fragment 'will achieve nutrient neutrality as part of their application.' 'Schedule of works (listed building)' is mapped to Arboricultural Method Statement text, and there is no such listed-building item. 'Sunlight to gardens/amenity space' is a fragment of B20 Private open space (all new dwellings). 'Drainage Strategy / SuDS' and 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' are fragments of FRA and general reasoning text, not standalone requirements.
issues.evidence: A8: 'Net increase in overnight population on a wastewater system in the river Stour catchment (including non-mains drainage)... e.g. Lenham'

issues.detail: Tab items include process text and fragments. 'Submission rules': file types and 10MB size limits (from three sources), the fragment 'Maidstone Council Affordable and Local Needs Housing July 2020.pdf A10:' (twice), the Kent minerals SPD reference, and the housing intensification advice note reference. 'Drawing / document standards': reasoning text ('Plans need to be viewed digitally...'). Policy-driven: bare fragments 'In a Special Protection Area (SPA)' (twice). Roof plan and 'Highways / access (visibility splays)' rows come from the general planning-application-guide page, not the validation list. That guide's 'You do not need to include a linear scale bar' also contradicts list item A2 ('All planning applications require scale bars').
issues.evidence: A2: 'All planning applications require scale bars'; guide tab item: 'You do not need to include a linear scale bar, but it is useful for online submissions.'

issues.detail: The same requirement text is repeated from three sources (current page, Swale 2024 PDF, old combined PDF). The nutrient neutrality / River Stour paragraph appears three times, 'preferred size is A1' twice, the 'Do not scale' wording three times, and the scale-bar rule about six times across tab items.
issues.evidence: Tab items sourced from maidstone.gov.uk page, swale.gov.uk 24.06.13 PDF and docs.maidstone.gov.uk combined PDF with near-identical text

summary: Grokbot's link is the current Maidstone validation checklist page, but the date is wrong: 'Published: 26 January 2026', not October 2026. About 17 of its 43 local items are missing (e.g. parking stress surveys, renewable energy, social value, BNG enhancement plan, water efficiency, Building for Life 12). Many rows come from superseded joint Swale/Maidstone PDFs, triggers are often content text or altered quotes, and app types are wrong (BNG under Householder despite 'excluding householder'; prior approval misuse).
